$schema_note: Frozen competency-question set for the GDPR KG foundation. Serialization of the signed-off 27-CQ set in methodology/competency_questions_refined_proposal.md. This file is the machine-readable source of truth that drives the Phase-4 SHACL derivation and the Phase-5 SPARQL suite.

header.title: GDPR KG Foundation — Frozen Competency Questions (27)
header.status: FROZEN (serialization only). The five previously-open CQ decisions were resolved by Zied; this file records the resolutions and does not re-open them.

field_legend.id: Stable handle used by the SPARQL/SHACL suite. Do not renumber.
field_legend.theme: A = information/transparency duties (Art 13 & 14); B = lawful basis & consent (Art 6 & 7); C = cross-cutting / integrative.
field_legend.question: The competency question in natural language.
field_legend.probe: The modeling decision the CQ is designed to test.
field_legend.eval_level: true = answered by a procedure/metric over the graph(s), NOT by a single SPARQL query (kept in the set because it exercises the integrative claim). false = one-CQ-one-SPARQL.
field_legend.draft_origin: Traceability to the first-pass draft CQ id(s).
field_legend.subparts: Present where a merged CQ keeps distinct probes as sub-parts.

resolutions.note: The six resolutions below were decided by Zied and are recorded here, not re-decided. They govern how the CQs are interpreted and how Article instantiation grounds normative nodes.

R1_merge_7_3_and_7_4.decision: Merge draft CQ-7.3 + CQ-7.4 into CQ-B8 (one right + two correlative controller duties). Both original probes are retained as sub-parts of CQ-B8.

R2_drop_old_6_6.decision: Drop old draft CQ-6.6 (article-6-local basis-grounding). It is subsumed by CQ-C2 (uniform grounding incl. LegalBasis & Consent), which generalises it across every normatively-defined node.

R3_evaluation_level.decision: Keep CQ-A9 (Art 13 vs 14 diff) and CQ-C8 (source coverage) as EVALUATION-LEVEL — each is answered by a metric/procedure over the graph(s), not by a single SPARQL query.

R4_granularity_point_level.decision: Granularity = POINT-LEVEL. Obligations (and other normative nodes) ground to the specific Point along Article -> Paragraph -> Point. Where a provision has no Point subdivision, grounding is to the Paragraph.
R4_granularity_point_level.grounding_basis: GDPRtEXT's ELI-based Point/SubPoint decomposition of the GDPR [pandit2018gdprtext, ESWC 2018].

R5_split_bundled_enumerations.decision: Bundled enumerations are SPLIT: an enumerated informational duty (e.g. the rights listed in Art 13(2)(b)) becomes one Obligation PER item, each grounded to the SAME Point. Item-level counting is therefore how CQ-A1/CQ-A2 coverage is measured.
R5_split_bundled_enumerations.rationale: Preserve per-right (per-item) traceability so each enumerated element is independently queryable and independently reviewable.
R5_split_bundled_enumerations.provenance_of_decision: Deliberate original design decision by Zied. NO prior-art source prescribes this split; it is NOT inherited practice. No citation is asserted for it (do not invent one).

R6_out_of_scope_referenced_provisions.decision: Article 9 and Articles 22, 44-49, 89 stay OUT OF SCOPE to model. They are referenced only as gdprkg:ReferencedProvision stub nodes and are never populated with normative structure.

competency_questions.question: Which information items must a controller provide when personal data are collected from the data subject, and to which Article 13(1)/(2) point is each grounded?
competency_questions.probe: Every 13(1)/(2) item is an information-disclosure Obligation grounded to its Point; per R5, bundled enumerations are split one Obligation per item so coverage is countable at item level.

competency_questions.question: Which information items must a controller provide when personal data are not obtained from the data subject, and to which Article 14(1)/(2) point is each grounded — including the two items unique to Art 14 (categories of data 14(1)(d); source of the data 14(2)(f))?
competency_questions.probe: Coverage + the Art-14-only items, each grounded at point level.

competency_questions.question: Which Article 13/14 information duties are conditional, and on what condition?
competency_questions.probe: Condition modeling + APPLIES_IF edges (legitimate-interests, transfer, consent basis, recipients-exist, etc.).

competency_questions.question: Under what circumstances do the Article 13 duties not apply, and to which obligations does the exemption attach?
competency_questions.probe: 13(4) 'already has the information' exemption + its attachment scope (blanket vs per-obligation is an OPEN legal-review item).

competency_questions.question: Under what conditions is a controller exempt from the Article 14 duties, and which obligations does each of the four 14(5) exceptions defeat?
competency_questions.probe: 14(5)(a-d) distinct triggers + per-obligation attachment.

competency_questions.question: When the 'impossible or disproportionate effort' exemption applies, what obligation remains in force?
competency_questions.probe: 14(5)(b) protective-measures duty arises inside the exception and is not defeated by it.

competency_questions.question: Does Article 13 (and Art 14) create substantive data-subject rights, or only duties to inform the subject about rights defined elsewhere?
competency_questions.probe: The decision to model 13(2)(b)/(c), 14(2)(c)/(d) mentions as information Obligations, not Right nodes.

competency_questions.question: Within what time limits, and on which triggering events, must Article 14 information be provided?
competency_questions.probe: 14(3)(a-c) as queryable timing structure (fixed limit via hasTimeLimit; event triggers via Condition + appliesIf).

competency_questions.question: How do the Article 14 duties differ from Article 13 (what 14 adds and omits)?
competency_questions.probe: Structured diff over the two article graphs; exercises the integrative claim (e.g. 14 lacks a 13(2)(e) statutory/contractual-requirement analogue; 14 adds 14(1)(d) categories and 14(2)(f) source).

competency_questions.question: Which lawful bases permit processing of personal data?
competency_questions.probe: 6(1)(a-f) as a LegalBasis structure, not six controller obligations.

competency_questions.question: Under what conditions is each lawful basis available?
competency_questions.probe: Per-basis necessity/balancing Conditions, linked to the LegalBasis (not merely co-grounded to the same Point).

competency_questions.question: Which lawful bases require a basis in Union or Member State law?
competency_questions.probe: 6(3) attaching specifically to (c) legal obligation and (e) public-interest as a traversable link from those bases, not free text.

competency_questions.question: Is the legitimate-interests basis excluded for public authorities acting in their tasks, and what does that exclusion attach to?
competency_questions.probe: 6(1)(f) 2nd sentence as a LegalEffect/Exception on the basis (LegalBasisLegitimateInterests).

competency_questions.question: What must a controller assess when processing for a new purpose, and which factors govern the compatibility assessment?
competency_questions.probe: 6(4) Obligation + the 6(4)(a-e) factors linked to it (factor-link is the probe).

competency_questions.question: What must a controller demonstrate when relying on consent?
competency_questions.probe: 7(1) demonstrate-consent Obligation.

competency_questions.question: What are the requirements for how a consent request is presented?
competency_questions.probe: 7(2) distinguishable / intelligible / plain language requirements.

competency_questions.question: What right does the data subject have over consent, and what duties does the controller bear in relation to withdrawal?
competency_questions.probe: 7(3) substantive Right (withdraw) + the two controller duties (inform before; make withdrawal as easy as giving), modelled as separate correlative nodes grounded in the same Point.

subparts.focus: Substantive right to withdraw consent at any time (7(3) sentence 1).
Controller duty to inform of the withdrawal right before consent is given (7(3) sentence 3).
Controller duty to make withdrawal as easy as giving consent (7(3) sentence 4).

competency_questions.merge_note: Merged from draft 7.3 + 7.4 per resolution R1; both probes kept as sub-parts.

competency_questions.question: Under what conditions is consent considered (not) freely given?
competency_questions.probe: 7(4) conditionality, linked to the Consent node / a validity assessment.

competency_questions.question: How is the legal effect of a consent declaration that breaches Article 7(2) represented?
competency_questions.probe: The LegalEffect pattern for 'not binding' vs. overloading Exception.

competency_questions.question: For a given article, what obligations, rights, conditions, and exceptions does it generate, and what provision is each grounded in?
competency_questions.probe: The core Article -> Paragraph/Point -> Obligation/Right path with grounding on every normative node.

competency_questions.question: For any normatively-defined node — including LegalBasis and Consent — can it be traced by a grounding relation (not merely a metadata attribute) to the specific provision that establishes it?
competency_questions.probe: The uniform-grounding fix (groundedIn on every GroundedConcept incl. LegalBasis and Consent). The single most important diagnostic CQ for the rebuild.
competency_questions.subsumes_note: Subsumes and generalises old draft CQ-6.6 per resolution R2.

competency_questions.question: For any obligation, which actor bears it, and for any right, which actor holds it?
competency_questions.probe: IMPOSES_OBLIGATION_ON / GRANTS_RIGHT_TO integrity.

competency_questions.question: For an obligation that references a specific third party (DPO, controller representative, supervisory authority, data source), can that party be identified and typed?
competency_questions.probe: Whether generic Actor nodes suffice or these need distinct Actor subclasses + obligation->actor edges.

competency_questions.question: Which obligations across different articles relate to the same privacy-domain concept (e.g. everything touching Consent, or international Transfer)?
competency_questions.probe: The domain layer as a cross-article connector via shared canonical domain nodes.

competency_questions.question: For any node, what is its provenance and current review status?
competency_questions.probe: Provenance/review layer present from the start (provenance + reviewStatus required on primary normative units; Condition/Exception inherit via parent).

competency_questions.question: For any obligation, is the point in time it must be performed represented in a queryable way?
competency_questions.probe: Temporal representation across articles (13 'at the time obtained'; 14(3) deadlines; 13(3)/14(4) 'prior to further processing').

competency_questions.question: Which parts of an article's source text are not yet represented as normative nodes?
competency_questions.probe: A coverage procedure over source_units, not one SPARQL query.
